summary: This program counts a coffee order's progress from 0% to 100% in steps of ten, printing each status update, then announces that the coffee is ready. It uses a do-while loop, so the status message is guaranteed to appear at least once.

lines.text: The do keyword marks the start of the block, and there is no condition here at all — the body runs before anything is evaluated, which is exactly what you want when the customer must be informed at least once.
Something inside the body has to move status toward the stopping point, otherwise the condition would stay true forever and the loop would never end.

The condition now sits at the end and is checked after each pass, so the loop repeats while the status has not yet passed 100. Note the semicolon: a do-while statement requires one here, unlike an ordinary while loop.
This line is outside the loop, so it runs once after the condition finally fails and the loop is done.
